newsitem.title: USA: Sony hits 12-month high in NYC.
newsitem.headline: Sony hits 12-month high in NYC.

text.p: Sony Corp's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) hit a 12-month high Monday, boosted by a weaker yen and a strong earnings outlook, traders said.
The Japanese electronics giant closed up 3-7/8 at 97-3/4, a 12-month record. Volume was more than twice normal levels.

Based on Sony's close of 11,300 yen on Tokyo and the exchange rate of the yen to the dollar, the ADRs finished 1-3/4 above where Sony ended in Tokyo, said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
Based on the ADR's performance, Sony "will at least start at the upside in Tokyo tonight," he said.
The yen's slump against the dollar has led to a surge in the stock of major Japanese exporters, such as Sony.
"There is just a great deal of enthusiasm about owning these things that have a lot of revenues that are not in yen," Kosmider said.
Analysts also expect Sony to report a 30 to 60 percent rise in operating profits for the first business quarter. The company will release results Thursday.
"The expectation is that they (the results) are going to be great," Kosmider said.
